The plot above illustrates each nutrient in the McDonalds dataset & the number of times in which the daily recommended value, as described the US FDA, was exceeded for each nutrient. There are 15 unique nutrients. This data was formed from ten random daily meal plans each of which contained eight random food items from the McDonalds menu. More details on how these meals were constructed & assembled are available earlier in Analysis IV. Moreover, the recommended daily values for each nutrient are available in the FDA_daily_nutrients variable.
By compiling the results across a sizable number of random daily meals, it can provide an idea as to how proficient a typical day's worth of meals at McDonalds is at providing a healthy amount of daily nutrients. Recall that the US FDA particularly recommends eating foods that are:

  • Higher in dietary fiber, calcium, & iron.
  • Lower in saturated fat, sodium, & added sugars.

Of the ten daily meal plans, at least three of them exceed the daily recommended quantity for at least 13 of the 15 nutrients. Furthermore, at least eight meal plans exceed the daily recommendations for nine of the nutrients. The two nutrients whose daily values were never exceeded in any daily meal plan were dietary fiber & iron. Moreover, daily recommendations of trans fat & vitamin C were only exceeded in four of the ten daily meal plans. Given this information, some conclusions can be made regarding a typical day's worth of McDonalds food items.

  • McDonalds meals usually fail to provide enough dietary fiber & iron for a balanced daily diet.
  • McDonalds meals often provide excessive amounts of calcium, calories, calories from fat, carbohydrates, protein, saturated fat, sodium, sugars, & total fat.
  • McDonalds meals sometimes provide too much cholesterol, trans fat, vitamin A, & vitamin C than a balanced daily diet typically requires.

Of the six nutrients specifically pointed out by the US FDA (dietary fiber, calcium, iron, saturated fat, sodium, & sugars), these results indicate that typical McDonalds meals are only sufficient in regard to one of them. More specifically, McDonalds meals typically provide ample amounts of calcium which is more desirable than the opposite according to the FDA; however, McDonalds meals typically provide insufficient amounts of dietary fiber & iron & excessive amounts of saturated fat, sodium, & sugars.
As such, it can be said that McDonalds meals typically fail to provide appropriate amounts of nutrients for balanced, healthy diets.

Analysis IV B - Manually Constructed Meal Plan¶

Next, a daily meal plan can be built by hand such that the recommended daily nutritional quantities are not grossly excessive or insufficient. This process was done manually & tinkered with until the entire collection of food items did not exceed any recommended daily nutritional values. Once more, a day's worth of meals consisted of eight items from the McDonalds items spread across three unique meals for breakfast, lunch, & dinner.

Through this, it can be determined as to how difficult assembling a balanced daily meal plan of McDonalds foods generally is & what nutrients consumers may need to look elsewhere for otherwise.

The meal plan that was assembled & analyzed below consists of: Hotcakes, an Iced Coffee with Sugar Free French Vanilla Syrup (Medium), a Diet Dr Pepper (Large), a Filet-O-Fish, Small French Fries, a Hamburger, a Dasani Water Bottle, & a Chocolate Chip Cookie.

In [14]:
#Find 8 food items across 3 meals
#BREAKFAST
breakf_items = ["Hotcakes", "Iced Coffee with Sugar Free French Vanilla Syrup (Medium)"]
#LUNCH
lunch_items = ["Diet Dr Pepper (Large)", "Filet-O-Fish", "Small French Fries"]
#DINNER
dinn_items = ["Hamburger", "Dasani Water Bottle", "Chocolate Chip Cookie"]

#collect all data for these items
daily_meal = orig_df[orig_df.Item.isin(breakf_items + lunch_items + dinn_items)]
#display(daily_meal)

From these aggregations, it is evident that these meals provide adequate amounts of many nutrients, but underwhelm for some others. More specifically, based on the daily recommended nutrient quantities from the US FDA, this collection of food items provides fairly adequate amounts of calories from fat, protein, saturated fat, sodium, sugars, total fat, & trans fat. Conversely, these items underwhelm appreciably when it comes to calcium, cholesterol, dietary fiber, iron, vitamin A, & vitamin C. Fortunately, these meals only account for 1,490 calories, so such a customer can eat additional items to try & consume more nutrients that these particular items lack in the context of a balanced diet; however, this might be challenging to do without consuming too much nutrients when it comes to those that these items are richer in such as calories from fat, saturated fat, sodium, & sugars.

When analyzed across the six nutrients particularly emphasized by the US FDA (dietary fiber, iron, calcium, saturated fat, sodium, & sugars), these meals are fairly rich in saturated fat (~ 93% of the recommended daily value), sodium (~ 92%), & sugars (~ 84%). Given that this meal only accounts for about 75% of a typical diet in terms of calories consumed, it provides slightly excessive amounts of saturated fat, sodium, & sugars, which might be indicative of unhealthy food options given that such levels of these nutrients are particularly discouraged by the FDA.
Moreover, these meals are quite insufficient in dietary fiber (~ 32% of the recommended daily amount), iron (~ 52%), & calcium (~ 46%), nutrients in which the FDA encourages people to consume more of.

As such, given the uneven proportions in nutrients, particularly of those emphasized by the US FDA, this daily meal plan leans more towards being unhealthy & unbalanced based on a typical diet; however, there is still enough room, in terms of calories, such that these imbalances can be righted, but consumers may need to go beyond McDonalds to find suitable food items. Moreover, for those trying to follow a healthier, more balanced diet, eating these eight items will likely make it more challenging for them to find healthier foods that can supplement these items without exceeding certain nutrients that these eight foods are relatively rich in.

In relation to Analysis IV A, in which ten random daily meal plans were assembled, this 11th meal plan seems to be a bit of an outlier given that it did not exceed any daily nutritional recommendations whereas all but two nutrients & their recommendations were exceeded across many of the former ten meal plans. This might be indicative as to how challenging it generally is to assemble a day's worth of meals from McDonalds that can generate a balanced diet in terms of nutrients.

The plots above display how much of each nutrient each of the eight items in the constructed daily meal plan account for. Of the 15 nutrients in the dataset, only ten were plotted here. In each of these pie charts, there was at least one item that accounted for zero percent of that nutrient's distribution across the entire daily meal plan.

  • These meals included: Hotcakes, an Iced Coffee with Sugar Free French Vanilla Syrup (Medium), a Diet Dr Pepper (Large), a Filet-O-Fish, Small French Fries, a Hamburger, a Dasani Water Bottle, & a Chocolate Chip Cookie.
  • If the figures above don't appear, reference the "Nutritional Distributions of the Constructed Daily Meal - Pie Charts.html" file.

The Filet-O-Fish accounts for the largest pie slice in the distributions of five of the ten nutrients (calories, total fat, cholesterol, protein, & calcium). Hotcakes accounts for the most of three other nutrients (carbohydrates, dietar fiber, & sugars). The Dasani Water Bottle item has no nutritional values across each of these ten nutrients.

  • For most (six) of these nutrients, the Filet-O-Fish, Hotcakes, & Hamburger contribute the most nutritional value to this day's worth of food.
  • For most (eight) of these nutrients, the Dasani Water Bottle & Diet Dr. Pepper (Large) contribute the least nutritional value to this day's worth of food.

Regarding the nutrients particularly emphasized by the US FDA, the Hotcakes contain a relatively large amount of sodium & sugars across the eight items. The Hotcakes also contain a relatively large amount of dietary fiber, calcium, & iron. The Hamburger & Filet-O-Fish also contain a notable amount of calcium, iron, & sodium. The Chocolate Chip Cookie is the biggest contributor of Sugars in this meal plan.
